title.zh: AI 交出 700 多份手稿，数学家为何分歧如此之大？
title.en: AI released 700-plus manuscripts. Why are mathematicians divided?

deck.zh: 10 月 6 日，OpenAI 公布内部模型生成的数学研究材料。有人把它看作科研加速的起点，有人呼吁停止合作。这两种反应，究竟在回答什么问题？
deck.en: On October 6, OpenAI released mathematical research generated by an internal model. Some saw an acceleration of discovery; others called for a boycott. What lies behind these different responses?

takeaway.zh: 本期重点读卡兹克《AI让数学再也回不去那个旧世界了。》，再对照 APPSO 的争议报道与数学家的原始声明。从事件本身开始，看看 AI 改变了哪一段研究，又把哪些问题推到了台前。
takeaway.en: Our lead reading is Kazike’s essay on AI’s transformation of mathematics, alongside APPSO’s reporting and mathematicians’ original statements. Start with the event, then follow what changes in research.

title.zh: 10 月 6 日，究竟发生了什么？
title.en: What happened on October 6?

navLabel.zh: 先看事件

text.zh:
10 月 6 日，OpenAI 在 GitHub 建立 openai/math 仓库，公开了一批由未发布的内部模型生成的数学手稿与证明材料。事情的起点，是公司现有的数学评测越来越难区分模型水平，于是把测试推进到尚未解决的研究问题上。对普通读者来说，最重要的变化是：AI 交出的开始包含对未知问题的论证，而不只是标准题的答案。

“数学手稿”可以先理解为研究论文的草稿：它要明确声称什么成立，列出成立的条件，再给出推导。公开草稿便于别人检查、讨论和接着研究，却不等于已经完成同行评审。仓库中的材料有不同的核验进度，也包含同一主结果的补充证明、推论或另一种证法，所以文件数不能直接当作突破的数量。

其中引人注目的方向包括：研究素数分布背后的黎曼 ζ 函数、寻找更快的矩阵乘法，以及四维空间中的挂谷问题。即使不掌握这些数学细节，也能理解它们为何引起关注：模型正在尝试研究者长期追踪的问题，给出的材料有机会被逐步核查，而非只能凭语言流畅度来相信。

发布也很快伴随纠错。最初的 722 份手稿，在三份撤回后变为本期采用版本的 719 份，仍归在 372 个成果家族中。乐观者看到的是机器探索的规模；谨慎者看到的是大量研究材料仍待审查。接下来的争论，正是从这两种观察同时成立开始的。
text.en:
On October 6, OpenAI published openai/math, a GitHub collection of mathematical manuscripts and proof artifacts generated by an unreleased internal model. Existing mathematics evaluations had become less informative, so the company expanded evaluation to open research problems. The significant change is what the model was being asked to produce: arguments about unresolved questions, beyond answers to established exercises.

A manuscript is a research draft. It states a claim and its assumptions, then presents an argument. Public release allows scrutiny and follow-up work; it is not the same as completed peer review. The collection includes materials at different verification stages, and several documents can belong to one result: companion arguments, consequences or alternative proofs.

Prominent examples concern the Riemann zeta function, connected to the distribution of prime numbers; faster matrix multiplication; and a four-dimensional Kakeya problem. Readers need not master the details to see the significance. AI is attempting questions researchers have pursued, producing arguments that can be examined beyond how convincingly they read.

Corrections followed release. The initial 722 manuscripts became 719 after three withdrawals; the version used here groups them into 372 result families. Optimists see the scale of machine exploration. Cautious readers see a large body of material still requiring scrutiny. The dispute begins with both observations being possible at once.

title.zh: 为什么这次值得重视：AI 开始提供研究路径
title.en: Why this matters: AI is contributing paths into research

navLabel.zh: AI 做了什么

text.zh:
过去谈 AI 做数学，常见场景是让它解一道已有答案的题，或把人写好的证明翻译成机器能检查的形式。开放问题没有随手可查的标准答案：系统需要找到可行的论证、处理障碍，并把结果写成别人能追问的材料。若这些论证成立，这就是研究能力的进展，不能因为作者是机器就抹去。

卡兹克那篇文章最有启发的一点，是把这种进展与反馈速度联系起来。在可以较快检验结果的领域，AI 能反复尝试、发现失败、改变路线；同样一段时间里，可探索的方向就可能增加。这个想法也解释了为什么数学与代码特别受关注：它们的一部分成果，能够接上自动检查。

但这里仍有一处需要补上：找到证明、把它写入形式系统、确认它对应原问题，是不同的工作。仓库发布的是一套评估与整理流程留下的成果。模型承担了实质性的论证生成，问题选择、既有文献、检查工具和发布筛选也参与其中。承认 AI 的贡献，与看见这些条件，并不冲突。

真正令人兴奋的前景，是研究者可以让模型探索自己暂时顾不过来的路径，再从中提炼有用的方法。变化因此不只是“一道题更快做完”，还可能是同一个人有能力比较更多方向。当然，公开的成功材料还不足以告诉我们，随便换一个研究问题，系统有多大把握成功。
text.en:
Earlier discussions of AI mathematics often centered on solving exercises with known answers or translating a human proof into a machine-checkable language. An open problem has no ready answer key. A system must find a viable argument, navigate obstacles and present something others can examine. Valid contributions to that process constitute research progress regardless of their machine origin.

Kazike’s most useful argument connects progress to the speed of feedback. Where results can be checked quickly, AI can attempt a route, encounter failure and try again. More directions become accessible within a given period. Mathematics and code attract attention partly because some outputs can be connected to automatic checks.

A missing step still matters: finding an argument, formalizing it and confirming that it addresses the intended problem are different jobs. The collection is the output of an evaluation and preparation process. The model contributed arguments; problem selection, earlier literature, checking tools and selection for release also shaped the result.

The prospect is larger than finishing one problem faster. Researchers could explore routes they previously lacked time to pursue, compare alternatives and extract useful methods. That is a substantive expansion of working capacity. A selected collection of successes, however, does not establish a general success rate for an arbitrary new research question.

title.zh: 反对者究竟在反对什么？
title.en: What are the objections actually about?

navLabel.zh: 分歧在哪里

text.zh:
APPSO 收藏文章《陶哲轩转发抵制声明，数学界和 OpenAI 彻底撕破脸》把另一面带进了视野：手稿中的错误、批量发布的方式，以及研究者对未来角色的担忧。它与卡兹克文章形成的张力很清楚——前者追问这次发布怎样影响数学共同体，后者更看重 AI 能力跃迁带来的可能性。两篇都比各自标题呈现的立场复杂。

这里需要先认识两个名字。人类数学协会（AHM）在 10 月 7 日明确呼吁数学家停止与 OpenAI 合作，认为这类发布把公司力量放在了理解数学之前。数学与人工智能咨询小组（AGMAI）则由一组独立学者组成：他们也反对用外界无法使用的内部模型测试前沿问题，但继续与实验室沟通，并提出公开、解释和资源支持的要求。

因此，“数学界抵制 AI”会把不同意见压成一种。陶哲轩博客转载的是 AHM 署名的客座声明；转载本身不等于由他领衔起草。AGMAI 提供建议，也不等于给这批成果背书。读到这些名字时，应当追问具体是谁、针对哪件事、提出什么要求。

APPSO 提到的撤回是实际的质量警讯，应该影响我们对未检查材料的信任；它却不是所有成果均被推翻的证据。同样，某份证明最终成立，也不能反过来证明发布与合作方式毫无问题。双方真正交叉的地方，是技术进展已经开始改变研究者的工作，而怎样衡量、怎样共同承担这种改变，还没有形成共识。
text.en:
The saved APPSO article brings another side into view: errors in the manuscripts, the release process and researchers’ concerns about their future roles. Its tension with Kazike’s essay is useful. One emphasizes consequences for the mathematical community; the other emphasizes the possibilities opened by AI capability. Neither is fully represented by its headline.

Two organizations matter. The Association for Human Mathematics, AHM, called on October 7 for mathematicians to discontinue work with OpenAI. It questioned whether this release model advances understanding. The Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence, AGMAI, is an independent group of scholars. It too objects to frontier research testing on inaccessible proprietary models, but continues discussions with labs and recommends better release practices and support for understanding.

“Mathematicians boycott AI” collapses these positions. Tao’s blog hosted an AHM-authored guest statement; that does not establish that he led its authorship. AGMAI’s advisory work is not an endorsement of the collection. The useful questions are who is speaking, what practice they object to and what they propose.

The withdrawals reported by APPSO are a real quality concern and should affect trust in unchecked material. They do not show that every result is false. Conversely, a valid proof does not settle every question about publication and collaboration. The common ground is that technical change is already affecting research work; the terms for evaluating and sharing that change remain contested.

title.zh: 有了 Lean，为什么争论还没有结束？
title.en: Why doesn’t Lean settle the dispute?

navLabel.zh: 怎样才算证实

text.zh:
先把 Lean 想成一种把数学定义、命题与证明写得足够精确的语言。它的证明内核负责检查：在给定假设下，这段推导是否符合规则。它的重要性在于，读者不用仅凭“作者说自己检查过”来建立信任，也可以运行对应的检查。

然而，检查通过回答的是“写进去的命题是否得到证明”。举一个入门例子：想证明“所有整数的平方都大于零”，却在代码里多加了“这个整数不等于零”的条件，后一个命题能够成立，原来那个命题却在零这里失败。机器没有失职；被检查的任务已经变了。实际研究中的差异会更隐蔽，因此原问题、自然语言手稿与形式化命题仍须逐项对应。

此外，一个证明即便正确，也可能重新发现了已有结论，或暂时没有让人看清方法。卡兹克把自动检查视为科研加速器，这一点值得重视；把整个科研过程的判断成本都算成一次检查的成本，就会低估文献核对、解释和应用所需的工作。形式化覆盖到哪一步，也必须具体说明。

这些工作并不注定永远只能靠人慢慢完成。Lean 内核的一份缺陷复盘已经记录了 AI 辅助查错的作用，模型也可以帮助搜索文献、比较命题和寻找反例。更合理的技术路线，是同时改进生成与检查，让“这份材料为什么可信”能够被下一位研究者直接利用。
text.en:
Think of Lean as a language for stating mathematical definitions, claims and proofs precisely. Its proof kernel checks whether an argument follows the rules under its stated assumptions. This gives readers a way to check corresponding artifacts beyond trusting an author’s assertion.

But a successful check concerns the statement actually encoded. Consider a simple example: someone intends to prove that every integer has a positive square, but adds “the integer is nonzero” in the formal statement. The revised claim is true; the original fails at zero. The checker has not malfunctioned. The task changed. Research-level differences can be much subtler, so the original question, manuscript and formal statement must still be matched.

Correctness also leaves other questions open. An argument may rediscover a known result, or provide little explanation of its method. Kazike is right to draw attention to fast feedback as an accelerator. Treating the entire cost of research assessment as the cost of one check, however, leaves out literature review, explanation and application. Formalization coverage also needs an explicit scope.

These jobs need not remain exclusively human. A Lean kernel postmortem records AI-assisted bug finding, and models can also assist literature search, statement comparison and counterexample discovery. The promising technical direction improves generation and scrutiny together, producing reasons for trust that another researcher can reuse.

title.zh: 证明便宜了，谁来承担理解的工作？
title.en: If proofs become cheaper, who supports understanding?

navLabel.zh: 工作怎样改变

text.zh:
设想一位研究生准备花几个月研究一个问题，突然发现 AI 已经公开了一份可能的证明。对学科来说，这或许是好消息；对他来说，原来的研究计划却要重排。他需要先确认结果，再决定改换方向、扩展结论，还是把证明中的新方法学会。得到答案和获得研究能力，并不发生在同一个瞬间。

这个场景解释了为什么“多发些成果总是好事”不足以结束争论。研究成果要通过讲解、讨论与使用，才能进入其他人的工作。若产出量增长得比消化能力快，注意力就会转向筛选和理解：哪些值得先读，谁来解释，做这些工作的人能获得什么支持与认可？

AGMAI 提出的一条具体办法，是让发布大量尚未被充分理解材料的实验室支持后续工作，并由既有的非营利学术机构决定资源怎样分配。研讨会、长期工作组、面向学生的讲解，都可以成为研究成果的一部分。这个建议的要点，是把“发布一个答案”与“帮助学科使用这个答案”连起来。

另一层问题是工具能否被广泛使用。公开一份证明，让别人能够核查；开放研究工具，让别人能够按自己的兴趣提出问题。两者都重要，作用却不同。我担心的未来是少数实验室不断出题、交卷，其他人只能接收；我更希望看到的，是更多研究者借助同类能力开展自己选择的探索。
text.en:
Imagine a doctoral student planning several months of work who discovers that AI has released a possible proof of the same problem. That may be good news for the field, while requiring a major change to the student’s project. They must check the result, then choose whether to change direction, extend it or learn its method. Receiving an answer and developing research ability happen on different timescales.

This illustrates why “more results must be better” does not end the argument. Explanations, discussion and use carry results into other people’s work. When output grows faster than the ability to assimilate it, attention shifts toward selection and understanding. Which results deserve attention first? Who explains them? How is that labor supported and recognized?

AGMAI proposes that labs support the assimilation of substantial output that is not yet well understood, with established nonprofit academic institutions directing funding decisions. Workshops, sustained working groups and exposition can help turn a released answer into usable knowledge.

Access raises a further question. A public proof lets others examine a result; accessible research tools let them pursue their own questions. Both matter in different ways. The worrying scenario concentrates agenda-setting and discovery inside a few labs, leaving others primarily to receive outputs. The preferable one expands the number of researchers able to explore directions of their own choosing.

title.zh: 艺术家曾经抵制 AI，这次会重演吗？
title.en: Will this follow the earlier resistance to AI in art?

navLabel.zh: 历史能说明什么

text.zh:
这种联想很自然：一个群体长期投入的专业能力，突然面对大规模自动化；一部分人兴奋，另一部分人担心职业与价值被削弱。艺术家与数学家都可能有这种感受。但要判断两场争议是否相似，不能只看“有人反对”，还要看他们反对的对象后来发生了什么变化。

先看更贴近数学的先例。1976 年，Appel 与 Haken 的四色定理证明使用计算机处理大量情形。四色定理说的是：平面地图只需四种颜色，就能让共享边界的地区颜色不同。争论不仅是程序会不会出错，也包括一个人无法逐项读完的计算，能否带来与传统证明相同的理解。Thurston 在 1994 年仍借它讨论数学中的理解；2005 年完成的形式化证明，则加强了可靠检查的基础。后来形成的是新的检查方法与信任方式，解释的需求并没有消失。

再看艺术领域。2024 年创作者的 AI 训练声明，针对的是未经授权使用作品。它提出的问题并不是“机器永远画不好”，而是作品如何被使用，以及创作者的生计。2025 年，华纳音乐与 Suno 宣布许可合作，强调相关使用中的创作者选择权。这个后续说明，采用 AI 与谈判合作条件可以同时发生；它并不能说明所有艺术家已经受益，或者早先的反对都失去了理由。

回到数学，结论的真假有相对严格的检查方法，艺术价值却没有同一种裁判；今天的 AI 还直接参与生成研究路线，影响也超出了早年的计算机辅助证明。可以借鉴的不是一条“先反对、后接受”的宿命，而是一种更具体的转变：把担忧落实为可检查的证明、可使用的工具、可讨论的署名与可持续的培养方式。
text.en:
The comparison is understandable. A profession built around difficult skills encounters automation at scale; excitement coexists with concern about work and value. Artists and mathematicians can share that experience. But “there was resistance” is not enough to establish the analogy. We must ask what was contested and whether those conditions subsequently changed.

A closer mathematical precedent is Appel and Haken’s 1976 computer-assisted proof of the four-color theorem: four colors suffice for a planar map when regions sharing a boundary must differ. Extensive computation raised questions about both reliability and understanding. Thurston still used the example in 1994 to discuss mathematical understanding. A formal proof completed in 2005 strengthened the basis for checking. New mechanisms of trust developed without eliminating the desire for insight.

In the arts, the 2024 AI training statement objected to unlicensed use of creative works and its effect on livelihoods. Its claim was not simply that machines could never produce good art. Warner Music Group and Suno’s 2025 partnership announcement emphasized licensing and creator choice. It illustrates that adoption and negotiation can coexist. It does not establish that all artists benefited or that earlier objections became groundless.

Mathematical truth has checking methods unlike judgments of artistic value. Today’s AI also generates research arguments, reaching beyond earlier computer-assisted computation. The useful lesson is therefore a concrete institutional adaptation, rather than inevitable surrender: checkable proofs, accessible tools, explicit credit and sustainable training can turn concerns into better terms of use.

title.zh: 数学家与 AI，怎样合作才不只剩“交卷与批卷”？
title.en: How can collaboration go beyond generating and reviewing proofs?

navLabel.zh: 未来的合作

text.zh:
把未来想成“AI 不断写证明，人类负责审核”，容易忽略研究的循环。一个证明会带出新的问题，失败的路线也可能留下方法；模型既可以帮忙找答案，也可以帮助提出问题、比较解释。因此，把“提问与意义永远属于人，执行永远属于机器”当作稳定分工，同样不可靠。

更有建设性的关系可以从一个具体研究任务出发：研究者说明想理解的现象，模型列出可能的路线；双方通过小例子、反例与文献排除不合适的方向；形成论证后，再把关键思路与检查材料整理成别人能用的形式。这里每一步都允许 AI 参与，也要求贡献能够被追问，而不是用一份看似完整的输出替代整个过程。

对学生，最需要保护的也许是练习判断的机会。我的建议是，允许用模型比较路线、检索背景，但要求学生解释关键假设，指出一个失败例子，并在条件改变后重新推理。这样才能区分“拿到了证明”与“学会了做研究”。Grant Sanderson 关于奖励解释工作的文章，以及 Álvaro Lozano-Robledo 对学生处境的讨论，都把注意力带向了这种能力的培养。

这还需要评价方式配合。如果学术奖励只认新结论的数量，写出清楚解释、整理机器证明、帮助别人掌握新方法，就容易成为没有回报的附属劳动。研究工具的进步应当扩大这些工作能够产生的价值。否则，即使成果更多，参与者也可能更难获得独立成长的空间。
text.en:
Imagining AI writing proofs and people reviewing them overlooks the cycle of research. Proofs suggest new questions; failed routes can leave useful methods. Models may help ask questions and explain arguments as well as solve them. A permanent boundary in which humans supply meaning and machines execute is therefore an uncertain foundation.

A more constructive relationship begins with an actual task. A researcher identifies something they want to understand; a model suggests possible routes. Examples, counterexamples and literature help eliminate unsuitable paths. Once an argument develops, its key ideas and checking materials are prepared for others to use. AI can participate throughout, while contributions remain open to questioning.

Students particularly need opportunities to develop judgment. I would allow model assistance with background and alternatives, while asking students to explain assumptions, identify a failed example and reason again when conditions change. That distinguishes obtaining a proof from learning to conduct research. Sanderson’s argument for recognizing explanatory work and Lozano-Robledo’s discussion of students both direct attention toward developing that capacity.

Academic incentives must support it. If recognition depends only on new-result counts, clear exposition, proof organization and teaching methods become under-rewarded support work. Better tools should increase the value of those activities too. Otherwise a larger volume of results can coexist with fewer opportunities for researchers to develop independently.

label.zh: Grant Sanderson · 怎样奖励解释工作
莱顿宣言 · 研究共同体的要求

title.zh: 跨过解题门槛之后，还有一道共同研究的门槛
title.en: Beyond solving problems: building a shared practice of research

navLabel.zh: 回到最初的问题

text.zh:
我推荐卡兹克那篇文章，是因为它让人看到：AI 的作用正在从辅助阅读和解题，延伸到研究成果的产生。这个变化值得兴奋，也值得逐项验证。APPSO 和数学家的声明补上了另一半：科研进展要通过人的讨论、工具的开放与方法的传播，才能真正扩展一个学科的能力。

所以，我不会把这场分歧写成“数学家输不起”，也不会据此宣布 AI 不该参与研究。我更看好持续合作，同时把解释、核查与资源支持放进成果发布的安排。机器能够贡献新的思想；研究者也应有条件检查它、改变它，并用它提出自己的问题。

接下来最值得观察的，是这些手稿有没有被独立复查、有没有催生新的研究，以及学生和普通研究者能否获得相应工具。它们会告诉我们，这次发布带来的究竟主要是更多文件，还是更多人能够继续探索的知识。下面几篇 Agent 专题，也沿着这条线展开：能力如何进入一项能够持续完成、能够回头检查的工作。
text.en:
Kazike’s essay is the lead recommendation because it makes a consequential shift visible: AI is extending from assistance with reading and exercises into the production of research. That warrants both excitement and specific verification. APPSO and the original statements supply another part of the story: discussion, access and transferable methods help new results expand a field’s capabilities.

I would neither dismiss the dispute as wounded professional pride nor conclude that AI should stay out of research. Continued collaboration is more promising, with explanation, scrutiny and support built into release practices. Machines can contribute ideas; researchers need the means to examine, alter and build on them.

The next evidence to watch is independent scrutiny, follow-on research and access for students and researchers beyond the labs. Those developments will reveal whether the release mainly adds documents or expands usable knowledge. The remaining features pursue a related question: how capabilities become sustained work whose steps can be inspected and understood.

label.zh: AGMAI · 对本次发布的回应
AGMAI · 对本次发布的回应

title.zh: 聊了两小时的 Agent，为什么会忘记最初的要求？
title.en: Why can an agent forget a request from two hours ago?

deck.zh: Pi 的两篇工程文章，拆开了长期对话中的两个问题：有限的工作记忆，以及反复读取历史的成本。
deck.en: Two Pi engineering articles examine limited working context and the cost of repeatedly processing conversation history.

takeaway.zh: 让 AI 连续改一个项目时，聊天还在、文件也在，它却可能忘记一条早先的约束。要理解这种情况，先要看看下一次模型请求里到底装了什么。
takeaway.en: A long coding conversation can retain its messages and files while the agent loses track of an earlier constraint. Understanding why starts with the input to its next model request.

title.zh: 上下文压缩，是一次会丢信息的交接
title.en: Compaction is a handoff that can lose information

navLabel.zh: 上下文压缩，是一次会丢信息的交接
navLabel.en: Compaction is a handoff that can lose information

text.zh:
Pi 是一种能读文件、改代码、调用工具的编程 Agent。它向模型发出下一轮请求时，需要带上系统规则、工具说明以及对话和执行记录。随着工作推进，这份材料不断变长；上下文窗口，也就是模型一次能处理的输入范围，却是有限的。聊天软件保存了记录，不代表模型每轮都能看到所有记录。

Pi 的做法是把较早的历史交给模型生成摘要，保留近期消息，再用这份较短的输入继续工作。这就是上下文压缩。可以把它理解为换班：交接单保留目标、进度和关键决定，完整档案则用于之后查找细节。被改动的是本轮能看见的材料，模型参数并没有因此重新训练。

用一个编者示例来看风险：用户说“把周刊做成中英文，先给我预览”，几小时后摘要只剩“完成周刊页面”。中文页面或许完成了，英文与预览范围却从工作记忆里消失了。后续 Agent 不是故意违背要求，而是在一份不完整的任务描述上继续推理。

所以，好的压缩要保留决定下一步行动的信息，尤其是尚未完成的要求、结论的出处和不确定性。摘要越短并不一定越好；能在必要时回到原记录，才有机会发现交接中漏掉了什么。
text.en:
Pi is a coding agent that reads files, changes code and calls tools. Its next model request includes instructions, tool definitions and a growing record of conversation and execution. The context window—the input a model can handle at once—is finite. A chat application can save more history than the model sees on any particular turn.

Pi summarizes older material while retaining recent messages, then continues with a shorter input. This is compaction. Think of a shift handoff: a brief carries goals, progress and key decisions, while original records remain available for details. The working input changes; the model’s parameters are not retrained.

Consider an editorial example. A user asks for Chinese and English versions of a weekly issue, initially as a preview. Hours later the summary says only “finish the issue page.” The Chinese page may be completed while the second language and preview scope disappear from working memory. Subsequent reasoning now starts from an incomplete task description.

Useful compression preserves what determines the next action: unfinished requirements, the basis for conclusions and unresolved questions. The shortest summary is not necessarily the best. Access to original records makes it possible to discover and correct a poor handoff.

highlights.en: A chat application can save more history

label.zh: Earendil · Pi 的上下文压缩

title.zh: 同一句“继续”，为什么有时特别贵？
title.en: Why can a short “continue” be expensive?

navLabel.zh: 同一句“继续”，为什么有时特别贵？
navLabel.en: Why can a short “continue” be expensive?

text.zh:
每次请求还会带出第二个问题：模型往往要重新处理很长的一段旧输入，而新增的内容只有几句话。提示缓存可以复用相同开头已经算好的注意力状态，从而减少重复计算。这里的“记住”，指的是复用计算结果，不是替模型增加一份可靠的事实记忆。

关键在“相同开头”。假设前一轮依次是系统规则、工具定义、聊天历史，下一轮只在末尾追加消息，前面的计算就有机会复用。若把中间的工具定义改了，后面的历史即使文字没变，也处在一个不同的前缀之后，需要重新处理。图中用颜色与虚线标出了这个分界。

这也解释了压缩与缓存之间的取舍：压缩让工作输入变短，却改写了历史，使第一次压缩后的请求需要重新建立后续缓存。频繁删改不一定省钱，长期保留全部材料又会占用上下文。系统要同时考虑事实是否完整、后续还要做多少轮，以及服务商实际能否保留缓存。
text.en:
A second problem is repeated work. Each request can contain a long stretch of old input with only a few new sentences. Prompt caching reuses attention state computed for an identical beginning, reducing recomputation. This is reuse of computational work, not an additional store of trustworthy facts.

The identical beginning is crucial. If a request contains instructions, tool definitions and history, appending a message may preserve reusable computation. Changing a tool definition in the middle changes the prefix for all later history, even if those later words stay the same. The diagram marks that boundary.

Compaction therefore trades a shorter working input against a rewritten prefix. The first request after compaction needs to establish the changed continuation again. Frequent edits need not save money, while retaining everything consumes context. Decisions need to account for information quality, remaining work and the provider’s actual retention behavior.

title.zh: 省下输入之后，也要算上返工
title.en: Count rework alongside input savings

navLabel.zh: 省下输入之后，也要算上返工

text.zh:
下面用一笔假设账单说明差别：原有输入 80k token，新增 4k；假设缓存读取单价是普通输入的十分之一，命中时按普通输入价格折算，相当于 12k 的费用，失效时则是 84k。两轮实际输入同为 84k，变化的是计费与重复计算，不是模型突然少看了七万多个 token。

但缓存命中率不是这项工作的最终成绩。一份摘要若漏掉英文版，哪怕之后每轮都很便宜，仍要为补做页面、重新审查和用户等待付出成本。反过来，为保留关键要求进行一次更好的压缩，可能先花一笔额外计算，却减少后续返工。

我会把长期记忆的质量放在三个问题上：它能不能保持原来的目标，能不能在新证据出现时改正旧判断，能不能找回结论依据。缓存帮助这些工作变得可负担；交接质量决定付出的计算是否仍在服务正确的任务。
text.en:
An illustrative bill makes the distinction concrete. Start with 80k old tokens and 4k new tokens. If cached reads cost one tenth of ordinary input, a hit costs the equivalent of 12k ordinary-input tokens; a miss costs 84k. Both requests contain 84k actual tokens. The difference is billing and recomputation, not that the model suddenly sees seventy thousand fewer tokens.

Cache-hit rate is not the final outcome. If a summary drops the English edition, inexpensive subsequent requests still leave translation, review and user waiting to be paid for. A better summary may incur additional computation now while avoiding later rework.

I would assess long-running memory by whether it preserves the goal, revises judgments when evidence changes and retains access to their basis. Caching helps make that work affordable. The quality of the handoff determines whether computation still serves the right task.

label.zh: Earendil · Pi 的上下文压缩

title.zh: Agent 做到一半断了，重启后能接着干吗？
title.en: Can an agent resume after crashing halfway through a task?

deck.zh: Pi Durable 为长时间运行的 Agent 保存工作状态。难点出现在它已经影响了外部世界，却还没来得及留下完整记录的时候。
deck.en: Pi Durable persists work for long-running agents. The difficult case arises when an external action has happened but its result has not yet been recorded.

takeaway.zh: 聊天断了可以重问；部署、写入或发信做到一半断了，却不能简单从头再来。本周收藏的技术手册把这个差别展示得很具体。
takeaway.en: An interrupted conversation can be restarted. A half-finished deployment, write or email cannot always be repeated. This week’s saved technical manual shows why.

title.zh: 先分清：Pi 是工作工具，Durable 是运行框架
title.en: Pi is a coding tool; Durable is an execution framework

navLabel.zh: 先分清：Pi 是工作工具，Durable 是运行框架
navLabel.en: Pi is a coding tool; Durable is an execution framework

text.zh:
10 月 1 日，Earendil 在发布 Pi 1.0 编程 Agent 的同时，推出了实验性的 Pi Durable。前者是人坐在终端前使用的工具；后者是给开发者构建长期 Agent 应用的框架。它把对话、工具调用和未完成任务存进存储，让新进程可以打开已有工作，继续处理。

为什么这件事值得单独研究？因为 Agent 的下一步常由模型根据当前记录决定。模型需要知道已经做过什么、哪些结果已确认，而不是只拿到一句“刚才断了，请继续”。持久化把这些事实留在模型之外，重启之后仍可读取。

手册中有一个强制终止进程的演示：报告获取被标记为 safe，部署被标记为 unsafe。重开同一存储后，系统可以重放报告获取；部署则返回中断信息，让后续流程判断已经发生了什么。safe / unsafe 在这里描述的是重放是否安全，不是工具本身好不好。
text.en:
On October 1, Earendil released the Pi 1.0 coding agent alongside an experimental package, Pi Durable. The former is a terminal tool used by a person; the latter is a framework for developers building long-running agent applications. It stores conversations, tool calls and unfinished tasks so another process can reopen existing work.

That matters because a model often chooses the next action from its current record. It needs established facts about completed actions and confirmed outcomes, rather than only “the process stopped; continue.” Persistence keeps those facts outside the model and available after a restart.

The manual demonstrates a forcibly terminated process with report retrieval marked safe and deployment marked unsafe. Reopening the store can replay retrieval, while deployment returns interruption information for subsequent handling. Here safe and unsafe describe replay semantics, not whether the tools are inherently good or bad.

label.zh: Earendil · Pi 1.0 与 Durable 发布说明

title.zh: 一封邮件，展示最棘手的时间空隙
title.en: An email exposes the difficult gap

navLabel.zh: 一封邮件，展示最棘手的时间空隙
navLabel.en: An email exposes the difficult gap

text.zh:
设想 Agent 已经请求邮件服务发送通知。邮件服务接受了请求，但本地进程在保存回执之前崩溃。重启后看不到“发送成功”，并不能说明邮件没有发出去。此时从头重试，可能重复发送；直接略过，又可能把一次真正失败的请求漏掉。

图中把本地记录与外部执行排在同一条时间线上。困难集中在远端已经执行、本地尚未确认的空隙。对这类动作，应用需要可查询的请求编号，或者远端支持的幂等键——同一请求重复提交，也只执行一次的标识。模型的自信程度无法填补这段缺失的事实。

这个例子也说明了框架的边界。把状态可靠保存下来，是恢复的基础；让外部动作不重复，还要与具体服务的接口配合。Pi Durable 不会因为保存了对话，就自动替所有外部服务实现恰好一次的执行。
text.en:
Suppose an agent requests an email notification. The mail service accepts it, but the local process crashes before saving the receipt. After restart, the absence of a success record does not show that nothing was sent. Retrying can duplicate a message; skipping can lose a genuinely failed request.

The diagram places local records and external execution on one timeline. The difficult interval is after remote execution but before local confirmation. Applications need a queryable request identifier or a provider-supported idempotency key: an identifier that lets repeated submissions represent the same action. Model confidence cannot replace missing state.

This also explains the framework’s boundary. Durable records provide the basis for recovery; preventing duplicate effects requires cooperation from the specific external service. Saving a conversation does not automatically implement exactly-once execution everywhere.

highlights.zh: 并不能说明邮件没有发出去
highlights.en: does not show that nothing was sent

title.zh: 持续运行有价值，是因为委托不必反复交代
title.en: Continuity matters because the work need not be handed over again

navLabel.zh: 持续运行有价值，是因为委托不必反复交代
navLabel.en: Continuity matters because the work need not be handed over again

text.zh:
把这一节与前面的上下文压缩放在一起，就能看清两种记录的分工。工作摘要保存“我们正在做什么、还欠什么”；持久执行记录保存“哪些动作已经发生、哪些结果还不确定”。前者丢失会让 Agent 忘记目标，后者丢失会让它误判世界的状态。

对于真正的长期任务，我更期待这样的体验：已确认的部分直接接着做；能够查询的结果先核对；只在出现新的选择或无法判断的状态时，让用户介入。这样既能减少反复交接，也保留必要的控制。每次都从头请示会削弱委托的价值，永不暴露不确定性则会让问题越积越多。

恢复机制可以让工作延续，但任务范围仍由原来的委托决定。用户要求做预览，重启之后就继续完成预览；发布仍然是另一项决定。持久化的价值是让任务更连贯，而不是让进程在恢复时悄悄得到更多权限。
text.en:
Together with compaction, persistence reveals two complementary records. A working summary carries the goal and remaining obligations; execution records carry completed actions and uncertain outcomes. Losing the first can derail the task. Losing the second can misrepresent the outside world.

For long-running work, I want confirmed work to continue, queryable outcomes to be checked and genuinely new choices or unresolved states to be surfaced. That reduces repeated handoffs while retaining control. Asking again at every step undermines delegation; concealing uncertainty lets problems accumulate.

Recovery should continue the original assignment. If the user requested a preview, the restarted agent completes that preview; publication remains a separate decision. Persistence makes a task more continuous. It does not silently expand its authority.

title.zh: Dream-RSI：让 AI 从走过的弯路里，学会安排下一次实验
title.en: Dream-RSI: using past experiments to plan the next attempt

deck.zh: 研究团队把代码优化的历史变成可重放的环境，再让 AI 改写探索策略。“做梦”省掉了什么，又没有省掉什么？
deck.en: The researchers turn code-optimization history into a replay environment, then use AI to revise the search policy. What does this “dreaming” save?

takeaway.zh: 想让一段程序跑得更快，Agent 可以生成许多版本、逐个测试。但预算有限，先试哪条路、在哪一条上继续投入，本身也是一道决策题。
takeaway.en: An agent can generate and test many versions of a program to make it faster. With a limited budget, choosing which route to try and which to pursue is a problem of its own.

title.zh: 它改进的对象，是“下一次试什么”
title.en: The target of improvement is what to try next

navLabel.zh: 它改进的对象，是“下一次试什么”
navLabel.en: The target of improvement is what to try next

text.zh:
Dream-RSI 是 Google、Google DeepMind、马里兰大学等机构合作开展的一项研究，关注 Agent 怎样安排探索。以代码优化为例：一次修改产生一个候选程序，测试得到结果，下一次再从某个候选继续修改。把父子关系留下来，就得到一棵探索树。树上不仅有最好的答案，也记录了通往它的分支和没有成功的尝试。

研究中的 AI 会改写负责安排探索的策略，比如挑选哪个候选继续、怎样分配并行尝试、什么时候停止一条路线。底层编码 Agent 保持不变。它类似让同一位实验员换一种实验安排：个人能力相同，投入的位置不同，也可能更早找到有用的结果。

论文把整个过程分成真实探索、历史重放和策略改写，再将新策略带回真实任务。旧经验因此可以帮助决定下一轮怎样收集经验，形成反馈循环。这就是“递归自我改进”在这项工作中的具体含义；它不要求每一轮都重新训练底层模型。

这个角度很值得关注。我们往往只问模型会不会写出好代码，却较少问一次任务里，试错预算是不是花在了合适的位置。Dream-RSI 把后一种能力变成了可以单独改进的对象。
text.en:
Dream-RSI, a collaboration involving Google, Google DeepMind, the University of Maryland and others, studies how agents organize exploration. In code optimization, a modification creates a candidate program, a test returns a result and a later attempt branches from one candidate. Recording parent-child relationships produces a search tree containing promising results as well as unsuccessful routes.

AI revises the policy that decides which candidates to extend, how to allocate parallel attempts and when to stop a route. The underlying coding agent remains fixed. The analogy is the same experimenter working from a better experimental plan: changing where effort goes can improve outcomes without changing individual capability.

The research alternates real exploration, historical replay and policy revision, then returns the revised policy to live tasks. Experience helps decide how to collect the next experience. That feedback loop is the concrete meaning of recursive self-improvement here; it does not require retraining the underlying model each round.

This is useful because coding capability and the allocation of a task’s trial budget are different questions. Dream-RSI makes the latter an explicit object of improvement.

highlights.zh: 底层编码 Agent 保持不变
highlights.en: The underlying coding agent remains fixed

title.zh: “做梦”为什么比重做实验便宜？
title.en: Why is replay cheaper than rerunning experiments?

navLabel.zh: “做梦”为什么比重做实验便宜？
navLabel.en: Why is replay cheaper than rerunning experiments?

text.zh:
假设已经测过一棵树：A 路线改善不大，B 路线更有潜力，C 路线失败。现在想比较两种策略——一种沿 A 反复深挖，另一种先看 A、B、C，再把预算给 B。如果这些访问过的节点都有记录，就可以重放选择顺序，读取已有结果，比较哪种策略更有效地利用预算。

便宜的原因在这里：无需为同一个已记录节点，再生成一次程序、再运行一次测试。重放仍有调度和策略评估的成本，但不必重复那部分昂贵的真实执行。图中的树用相同节点演示两条路线，帮助把“改策略”与“改程序”分开。

它的限制也很直观。旧树没有探索过的节点，并没有现成结果可供读取；历史本身还受旧策略影响，某些方向可能从未获得足够尝试。因而重放得出的优势，必须再到新任务中检验。否则，系统可能只是更擅长利用旧地图，并没有更擅长面对未知问题。
text.en:
Suppose a recorded tree contains a modest route A, a promising route B and a failed route C. One policy repeatedly pursues A; another surveys all three before concentrating on B. Where visited nodes already have recorded outcomes, their choice sequences can be replayed to compare the use of a limited budget.

The saving comes from avoiding regeneration and retesting of already recorded candidates. Scheduling and policy evaluation still cost something, but the expensive underlying experiment need not be repeated for that node. The illustration uses the same tree to separate changes in search policy from changes in a program.

An unvisited node has no stored answer. History also reflects the old policy’s choices, including directions that received little attention. A replay advantage therefore needs testing on new tasks. Otherwise the system may become better at navigating an old map without becoming better at exploring unknown terrain.

title.zh: 一次实验，读出两种不同的收益
title.en: One experiment, two different gains

navLabel.zh: 一次实验，读出两种不同的收益

text.zh:
项目用 Lasso 求解程序做了一组实验。Lasso 是一种通过惩罚系数大小来筛选变量的回归方法；这里要优化的，是求解程序的运行速度。实验分别记录寻找优化程序时的调用投入，以及所得程序在六个留出数据集上的平均运行时间。后者用来观察优化是否能延续到未参与同阶段策略筛选的数据。

在 Gemini-3.7-Flash 这一组中，固定探索使用 3,200 次调用，Dream-RSI 使用 1,879 次，约少 41%。得到的程序平均运行时间，则从 2,516.7 ms 降到 2,350.6 ms，约低 6.6%。前者是探索过程的投入，后者是产物的性能：这是两笔不同的账，不能合并成“AI 总体快了几倍”。

它支持的判断是，在该任务与设置下，改进探索方法可以少做一些昂贵尝试，同时找到表现更好的程序。这里采用作者报告的数据，没有独立复跑；完整成本还需要考虑策略优化等开销。

更远一点的启发是：AI 不只可以做工作，也可以改进自己组织工作的方式。但目标必须能被准确评价。优化运行时间的反馈相对明确；如果换成“写一篇好文章”，只用字数或产出速度打分，就很可能把策略训练到错误方向上。这正是我会持续关注的下一道难题。
text.en:
The project tests programs that solve Lasso, a regression method that penalizes coefficient size to select variables. The aim is to improve solver speed. It records discovery calls separately from average runtime on six held-out datasets, testing whether improvements carry into data not used for policy selection at that stage.

For Gemini-3.7-Flash, fixed exploration used 3,200 calls versus 1,879 for Dream-RSI, roughly 41% fewer. Average program runtime fell from 2,516.7 ms to 2,350.6 ms, about 6.6%. These measure different things: the investment in exploration and the performance of its output. They cannot be collapsed into one general speed multiplier.

Under those settings, a better exploration policy can reduce expensive attempts while finding a better program. These are the authors’ reported results, not an independent rerun. Full costs also need to include policy optimization and other overhead.

The broader possibility is that AI can improve how it organizes work. Evaluation remains crucial. Runtime offers relatively clear feedback. For “write a good article,” a score based on length or output speed can reward exactly the wrong behavior. Whether the target captures what matters is the next question I would watch.

title.zh: PANDA：一群 Agent，怎样组队才有意义？
title.en: PANDA: how should a group of agents form a useful team?

deck.zh: 这篇论文把目光放在协作基础设施：找到合适的伙伴，按任务组织通信，并在成员失联时继续工作。
deck.en: This paper studies collaboration infrastructure: finding suitable partners, organizing communication around a task and continuing when a participant fails.

takeaway.zh: 一个 Agent 会搜索，另一个会算数据，第三个能检查代码。把它们接到同一个群里，并不会自动形成团队；它们还需要知道该找谁、交接什么，以及谁掉线后怎样补位。
takeaway.en: One agent searches, another analyzes data and a third checks code. Putting them in a shared conversation does not automatically create a team. They need discovery, handoffs and a way to replace missing participants.

title.zh: 先找到伙伴，再建立小团队
title.en: Find collaborators, then form a small team

navLabel.zh: 先找到伙伴，再建立小团队
navLabel.en: Find collaborators, then form a small team

text.zh:
PANDA 是由美国东北大学研究者提出的多 Agent 架构。它考虑的场景是：大量 Agent 由不同主体维护，各有能力与工具，需要临时组合完成任务。若所有发现、调度和消息都经过一个总服务，负担会随规模增长，故障也容易影响其他任务。

PANDA 的办法是把“认识有哪些伙伴”与“这一组怎样干活”分开。节点维护本地能力索引，用来寻找协作者；选出小团队后，再建立任务内的通信。这样，一个小组讨论具体问题，不需要每次都让整个集体参与。

原图画的是一个节点内部的职责：Registry 保存伙伴信息，Team Manager 组织任务，Agent Backend 连接实际执行者，故障检测负责发现异常。去中心化并不是不要管理，而是把管理分散到节点和临时团队中。对于需要跨组织使用不同工具的 Agent，这比无限扩大一个总指挥更有想象空间。
text.en:
PANDA is a multi-agent architecture proposed by Northeastern University researchers. It considers a large population of independently managed agents with different tools and capabilities, assembled into temporary task teams. Routing discovery, scheduling and messages through one service can create a bottleneck and a common point of failure.

The design separates discovering available collaborators from communication within a selected team. Nodes maintain local capability indexes to find partners; a small team then establishes its task communication. A group discussing a specific problem need not involve the entire collective every time.

The source diagram shows responsibilities inside one node: a registry for peers, a team manager, a backend connecting the actual agent and failure detection. Decentralization redistributes management rather than eliminating it. That is an interesting direction for agents using capabilities across organizational boundaries.

title.zh: 组织结构要跟着任务走
title.en: Let the task determine the structure

navLabel.zh: 组织结构要跟着任务走
navLabel.en: Let the task determine the structure

text.zh:
论文支持星形、链式与网状协作。星形有一个团队内的汇总者，适合并行取材；链式按顺序交接，适合后一步依赖前一步结果；网状允许成员反复讨论，能增加交叉检查，也会增加通信。图里的字母只代表任务角色，不代表不同模型一定更聪明。

用本期数学专题做一个编者例子：一人查 OpenAI 发布说明，一人读 AHM 与 AGMAI 原声明，一人检查历史类比，最后汇总。这种分工的价值，是取得不同类型的证据。如果三个人都只读同一篇报道，再分别复述一次，一致意见仍可能来自同一个省略或错误。

因此，增加 Agent 数量之前，需要先问它会带来哪一种额外能力或材料。对单一、短小的任务，多一轮交接就可能只增加等待与误解；对需要不同专长和来源的任务，清楚的分工才有机会扩大一个人的工作范围。
text.en:
The paper supports star, chain and mesh orchestration. A star uses a team-level coordinator and suits parallel collection; a chain suits ordered dependencies; a mesh supports repeated discussion and cross-checking at additional communication cost. The diagram’s letters are roles, not an intelligence ranking.

Consider this issue as an editorial example. One participant examines OpenAI’s release, another reads AHM and AGMAI, and a third checks historical analogies before synthesis. The value comes from obtaining different kinds of evidence. Three agents paraphrasing the same report can still inherit one shared omission.

Before adding an agent, ask what additional capability or material it contributes. For a short, self-contained task, another handoff may add only delay and misunderstanding. Where expertise and evidence differ, clear division of work can expand what one person can accomplish.

title.zh: 团队能继续运行，还不等于它答对了
title.en: A team can keep running and still answer incorrectly

navLabel.zh: 团队能继续运行，还不等于它答对了
navLabel.en: A team can keep running and still answer incorrectly

text.zh:
PANDA 还研究成员崩溃、断网或协作流程出错后的恢复。系统能够发现受影响的任务，重新安排或更换执行者。它在 HotPotQA 这种需要结合多篇资料回答问题的测试上报告完成率与效率；其中“完成”，按论文定义，是产生了答案，不要求答案正确。

这个定义很关键。一位成员失联，可以通过超时和替换处理；三位成员都误读了同一份资料，却可能在系统里表现为一次非常顺畅的完成。下面的证据图把两件事分开：消息是否都到达，回答是否有足够的独立依据。

论文中的信任网络也主要用来约束谁能与谁合作，并不替代内容核查。我的期待是，这类基础设施让我们更容易组织真正互补的 AI 工作，而不是把角色数量当成质量保证。团队的价值，应当体现在补上了哪份证据、发现了哪个错误，或完成了单个 Agent 难以完成的任务。
text.en:
PANDA also studies recovery from crashes, network faults and failures in orchestration. Affected work can be replanned or reassigned. Its HotPotQA evaluation—a benchmark requiring information from multiple documents—reports completion and efficiency. The paper defines completion as producing an answer, regardless of whether that answer is correct.

That distinction matters. A missing member can be detected and replaced. Three members misreading the same source may look like a smoothly completed task. The evidence diagram separates whether messages arrive from whether a conclusion has independent support.

The paper’s trust network also constrains eligible collaborators; it is not a substitute for checking content. I hope this infrastructure makes complementary AI work easier to organize. Team quality should be visible in an added source, a discovered error or a task beyond the capacity of one agent, rather than in the number of assigned roles.

highlights.zh: 产生了答案，不要求答案正确
highlights.en: producing an answer, regardless of whether that answer is correct

text.zh: 让编码 Agent 通过 MCP 检查应用行为与二进制，沿着证据理解一个功能怎样实现。
text.en: Connect a coding agent to application and binary inspection through MCP, tracing how a feature works.

use.zh: 适合分析应用机制与兼容性问题。
use.en: For studying application behavior and compatibility.

note.zh: 分析能力取决于目标类型和本地工具环境。
note.en: Capabilities depend on the target and local analysis tools.

text.zh: 把设计工具、组件、学习资料与设计工程师放在一个可浏览的资源目录里。
text.en: A browsable directory of design tools, components, learning resources and design engineers.

use.zh: 适合找参考，再回到真实项目里试用。
use.en: For finding references to try in a real project.

note.zh: 目录推荐不等于与你的技术栈匹配。
note.en: A directory listing does not establish fit with your stack.

text.zh: 把 Agent 的身份、规则、记忆与技能写进 Git 仓库，用版本管理保留修改过程。
text.en: Keep an agent’s identity, rules, memory and skills in a Git repository, with versioned changes.

use.zh: 适合需要审查与协作的 Agent 配置。
use.en: For agent configurations that need review and collaboration.

note.zh: Git 的回滚只作用于仓库，不撤销已发生的外部动作。
note.en: A Git revert affects the repository, not completed external actions.

text.zh: 让 Agent 从统一入口发现并调用工具，提供 Skill、MCP 与 CLI 接入方式。
text.en: A shared entry point for agents to discover and call tools through skills, MCP or a CLI.

use.zh: 适合先验证一个具体的跨工具任务。
use.en: For testing a specific task across tools.

note.zh: 采用前核对计费、工具权限和数据流向。
note.en: Check billing, permissions and data flows before adopting it.

text.zh: 在桌面端给不同 Agent 配置指令和工作区，让它们交接任务、共享文件。
text.en: Give desktop agents separate instructions and workspaces, with task handoff and shared files.

use.zh: 适合尝试在本机协调多个工作角色。
use.en: For experimenting with several local work roles.

note.zh: 模型服务的使用费用和权限另行计算。
note.en: Model-service costs and permissions are separate.

text.zh: 把浏览页面与 Claude Code、Codex 任务放在同一个窗口，减少页面和项目之间的切换。
text.en: Bring browsing and Claude Code or Codex tasks into one window, connecting pages with project work.

use.zh: 适合边阅读、边把线索送进项目。
use.en: For moving a reading into project work.

note.zh: 区分普通浏览、只读分析与会修改项目的任务。
note.en: Distinguish browsing, read-only analysis and project edits.

text.zh: 让人和 Agent 都更方便地阅读、搜索与使用产品文档，连接文档和 API 工作流。
text.en: Help people and agents read, search and use product documentation alongside API workflows.

use.zh: 适合检查自家文档的可检索性与可操作性。
use.en: For examining whether your documentation is searchable and actionable.

note.zh: 先保证文档内容准确，再扩展自动化。
note.en: Establish content accuracy before expanding automation.

text.zh: 给 Agent 一台独立的 Debian 电脑，并提供远程连接和控制其他设备的硬件入口。
text.en: A dedicated Debian computer for agents, with remote access and hardware connections to other devices.

use.zh: 适合关注常驻任务与设备控制的人。
use.en: For readers exploring persistent tasks and device control.

note.zh: 预售产品；价格、交付时间与兼容性以官网为准。
note.en: A preorder product; confirm price, delivery and compatibility on its site.

text.zh: 在原生 macOS 窗口中管理虚拟 iPhone，查看设备库、配置和启动状态。
text.en: Manage virtual iPhones in a native macOS window, with a device library, settings and lifecycle controls.

use.zh: 适合已有 vphone-cli 的 iOS 研究环境。
use.en: For iOS research environments already using vphone-cli.

note.zh: 有硬件、系统与研究虚拟机环境要求，先读安装说明。
note.en: Read the hardware, OS and research-VM requirements first.

text.zh: 把多个编程 Agent 的对话、代码差异与 Git 协作放进一个开源图形控制台。
text.en: An open-source graphical workspace for coding-agent threads, diffs and Git collaboration.

use.zh: 适合希望集中查看编码任务的人。
use.en: For keeping coding work visible in one place.

note.zh: 它组织工作流；模型账户和 token 消耗仍需单独考虑。
note.en: It organizes work; model accounts and token usage remain separate.

title.zh: 把反复犯的错，写成下一次会失败的检查
title.en: Turn recurring mistakes into failing checks

text.zh: /correct 讨论的是编程 Agent 反复犯同一种错时，怎样把纠正留下来：把约束写进 lint、类型检查或测试。下一次即使模型忘了口头提醒，执行检查仍会给出具体反馈。它把“记住教训”变成了工作环境的一部分，适合那些能清楚描述失败条件的错误。
text.en: The /correct proposal turns recurring coding mistakes into lint rules, type checks or tests. Even when an agent forgets a verbal correction, the environment can report the same concrete failure. This preserves feedback where the failure condition can be stated clearly.

title.zh: 文件名会变，项目约束仍要说清楚
title.en: Names change; project constraints still need clarity

text.zh: 这篇收藏讨论 CLAUDE.md、AGENTS.md 与 Agent 运行环境的定制。这类文件承担的是项目交接：告诉 Agent 怎样构建、怎样验收、哪些约束不能漏。真正有价值的内容是能让它开始工作的具体信息；文件名与加载方式则需要随所用工具一起确认。
text.en: This reading discusses CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and customization of the environment around an agent. These files serve as project handoffs: how to build, how to validate and which constraints matter. Useful instructions make work startable; filenames and loading behavior remain tool-specific.

title.zh: EmbeddingGemma 2：让不同模态进入同一检索空间
title.en: EmbeddingGemma 2: one retrieval space across modalities

text.zh: Google 的模型卡确认文本、图像、视频与音频可以映射到同一 768 维空间，并允许按需加载编码器。它值得从一个自己的资料库任务试起：用文字找到相关图片或录音。先评估召回结果与设备负担，再判断是否适合长期使用。
text.en: Google’s model card describes text, image, video and audio embeddings in a shared 768-dimensional space, with selectively loaded encoders. Try a personal-library task, such as finding an image or recording from text, then evaluate retrieval and device overhead.

title.zh: Jev 的应用目录又长了一点
title.en: The Jev application list keeps growing

text.zh: 本条收藏记录 awesome-jev 从 583 到 591 条的巡检，新增方向涉及 bisect、审核与安全扫描。这里更值得逐项看的是：决策层在哪里接入、判断之后由谁执行。目录规模是原帖的时点记录，不代表每个项目都已经成熟。
text.en: The saved inspection note records awesome-jev growing from 583 to 591 entries, including bisect, moderation and security work. Examine where each decision layer connects and what executes afterward. The count is a snapshot, not a maturity rating.

title.zh: DEX #366：个人 Agent 需要怎样的电脑
title.en: DEX #366: what computer does a personal agent need?

text.zh: DEX 把个人 Agent、云端电脑和 AI 电脑放在一起，很适合比较任务住在哪里：随身设备、常驻主机，还是临时云桌面。选择环境时，先想任务是否要持续运行、要访问什么资料、故障后怎样接手；再看硬件和服务。
text.en: DEX groups personal agents, cloud desktops and AI computers. Compare where a task lives: a portable device, an always-on host or a temporary cloud desktop. Start with persistence, data access and recovery needs before choosing hardware or services.

title.zh: 16 款产品，反复出现的是记忆与主动性
title.en: Across 16 products, memory and initiative recur

text.zh: Founder Park 的产品合集覆盖 Personal Agent、垂直助手和记忆工具。适合当一张候选清单来浏览，先选与你眼下任务相邻的一款。主动提醒能否帮忙，要看它记住了什么、何时打断你，以及能否让你检查和修正。
text.en: Founder Park’s roundup spans personal agents, specialist assistants and memory tools. Use it as a candidate list and try one adjacent to a current task. Useful initiative depends on what a tool remembers, when it interrupts and whether you can inspect and correct it.

title.zh: Thin Is In：界面变薄以后，控制留在哪里
title.en: Thin Is In: where does control live in a thinner interface?

text.zh: 《Thin Is In》把持续存在的 Agent 与更轻的交互界面联系起来。过去需要打开应用、点击多个入口的工作，可能收敛为一句委托。由此产生的新设计题是：操作入口少了，任务进度、所用材料和用户接管的位置，应该怎样保留下来？
text.en: Thin Is In connects persistent agents with lighter interfaces. Work that once required opening an app and navigating several controls may begin with a short request. That creates a design question: where do progress, source material and opportunities to take over remain visible?

title.zh: AIGC Weekly #191：本期只读到公开节选
title.en: AIGC Weekly #191: a partial reading

text.zh: 已缓存的公开部分涉及 Personal Agent、AI 反编译与跨设备工作。阅读流标注目前只收到了约 21% 内容，因此这里只保留这份节选的线索，不把它写成完整一期的结论；想读全篇，可以回到原订阅渠道。
text.en: The cached portion covers personal agents, AI decompilation and cross-device work. The stream reports roughly 21% coverage, so this note retains the excerpt’s threads without presenting a verdict on the entire newsletter. The full issue belongs in its subscription channel.

title.zh: AI 越来越常用，是否就说明投入越来越值得？
title.en: Does more AI usage mean better value?

text.zh: 卡兹克对照 A16Z 的两份报告，观察 AI 的使用频率、付费与消费集中。它提供了从“模型又强了多少”转向“人们怎样使用 AI”的视角。读这类数据时，我会把使用者、付费者与整体人群分开：付费增长说明需求，却还需要任务完成、节省时间和持续使用的数据，才能解释用户获得了什么价值。
text.en: Kazike compares two A16Z reports on usage frequency, payment and concentration of spending. The useful shift is from model capability to how people use AI. Users, paying users and the general population are different denominators. Spending indicates demand; completed tasks, time saved and continued use help explain the value delivered.

title.zh: 手指的间隙：一个看得见的芝诺悖论
title.en: The gap between fingers: seeing Zeno’s paradox

text.zh: 原帖把指缝不断对半的过程拍给孩子看。它提醒我，解释一个概念不一定先搬出复杂符号。下面是编者自己的等比图解：无穷多个剩余步骤，也可能有有限的总和；‘步骤无穷’本身，并不能推出‘时间无穷’。
text.en: The original post shows a child a finger gap repeatedly halving. Explanation need not begin with complicated notation. Our geometric-series sketch below makes one point: infinitely many remaining steps can have a finite sum; infinitely many steps alone do not imply infinite time.

title.zh: 《动手学大语言模型》：把图解当成学习路径
title.en: Hands-On Large Language Models: learn through diagrams

text.zh: Jay Alammar 与 Maarten Grootendorst 的《动手学大语言模型》，用图解和代码连接模型原理与实际应用。它适合补齐本期工程专题背后的基础：文本怎样变成 token，向量怎样支持检索，一次生成怎样接着已有输入继续。把机制看明白，再回头读产品宣称，更容易判断变化发生在哪一层。
text.en: Jay Alammar and Maarten Grootendorst’s Hands-On Large Language Models connects model concepts to applications through illustrations and code. It provides useful background for this issue: tokens, vector retrieval and generation conditioned on earlier input. Understanding the mechanism makes it easier to locate what a product claim actually changes.

title.zh: 准黎曼：固定的零点边界
title.en: Quasi-Riemann: a fixed zero-free boundary

navLabel.zh: 准黎曼

text.zh: 主手稿报告 7/8 右侧的无零点结论，并有同家族的 11/12 伴随证明。它们不等于完整黎曼猜想。这个例子的意义，是 AI 提供了可追查的研究论证；该论证能否完全成立，仍要按具体命题与证明来核验。
text.en: The main manuscript reports a zero-free region to the right of 7/8, with an 11/12 companion proof. Neither settles the full Riemann hypothesis. The case illustrates traceable research arguments, whose validity still depends on scrutiny of their exact statements and proofs.

title.zh: 矩阵乘法：指数上界，不是训练速度
title.en: Matrix multiplication: an exponent bound, not training speed

navLabel.zh: 矩阵乘法

text.zh: 手稿报告复数域的指数上界 9/4，并保留任意正 ε 的条件。下图只比较渐近主导项的增长；不能从 4.76 倍增长因子，推导出某张显卡或某个模型的实测加速。
text.en: The manuscript reports an exponent bound of 9/4 over complex numbers with an arbitrary positive epsilon. The illustration compares asymptotic leading growth, not measured acceleration of a GPU or model.

title.zh: 四维挂谷：维数与体积是不同指标
title.en: Four-dimensional Kakeya: dimension and volume differ

navLabel.zh: 四维挂谷

text.zh: 手稿报告四维空间中含各方向单位线段的集合具有完整 Hausdorff 维数。二维方向图只是入门示意，不展示四维证明，也不能用来宣布集合必须具有正体积。
text.en: The manuscript claims full Hausdorff dimension for a set containing a unit segment in every direction in four dimensions. The two-dimensional sketch is an introduction, not the proof or a claim of positive volume.
